name: Button
intent: Triggers an action. One strong brand Button per view.
usage: Pick an emphasis and an intent. Use one strong brand Button per view for the main action. Use subtle (the default) for quieter paths like cancel or back, and minimal for low-emphasis actions. Intent danger is only for work that cannot be undone. Only these pairs exist: strong with brand or danger, subtle with neutral, minimal with neutral, brand or danger. Accessibility is built in: native button, focus ring, loading and disabled states, and a label for icon-only buttons. See contracts/button.json for the full contract.

emphasis.note: How loud the Button is. strong is filled, subtle has a border, minimal has neither.

intent.note: Color role. Allowed pairs: strong with brand or danger (intent is required with strong); subtle with neutral; minimal with neutral, brand or danger. Leave both out for subtle neutral.

size.note: Heights 28 / 36 / 44 (control scale). Inside a ButtonGroup the group sets size. Without a size it is md. A surrounding Density changes these sizes through the density tokens (Default values shown).

iconSize.note: Icon size, 16 / 20 / 24 / 32. Leave out to follow the Button: 16 on sm, 20 on md and lg. Use a larger icon on an icon-only lg Button where the icon alone carries the action, like a phone footer.

iconOnly.note: Square button. Requires label for a11y; label is visually hidden.

toggle.note: Toggle on, for neutral subtle and minimal Buttons: brand tint and border, with aria-pressed. With aria-expanded (a button that shows or hides a panel, like the Toolbar Filters button) only the look changes.

useWhen: Submit, confirm, open, create, navigate to an action.
doNot: Do not use for in-text navigation (use Link).
Do not put two strong brand Buttons in one view.
Do not pair an emphasis and an intent outside the allowed pairs (no strong neutral, no subtle brand or danger).
Do not set iconSize larger than lg on a Button with a label; big icons are for icon-only Buttons.
a11y: loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled, keeps width and full color, and ignores clicks. It does not look disabled.
iconOnly needs children as accessible label.
toggle sets aria-pressed, unless the Button already has aria-expanded.

items.caption: Tab here to see the focus ring

examples.title: Strong brand
examples.usage: The main action. Use one strong brand Button per view. Show sm, md and lg when hierarchy or density changes.

examples.title: Subtle
examples.usage: The default. Use subtle for cancel, back, or other paths that should stay quieter than the strong brand Button.

examples.title: Minimal
examples.usage: Use minimal for quiet actions in toolbars, empty states, or dense screens where a filled button would feel heavy.

examples.title: Minimal brand and danger
examples.usage: A quiet action in the brand color, like Add row, or a quiet remove among other actions. Use minimal danger where a strong danger Button would be too loud, and still confirm costly work.

examples.title: Strong danger
examples.usage: Use strong danger only for actions that cannot be undone, like delete. Ask the user to confirm when a mistake would be costly.

examples.title: With icons
examples.usage: Put an icon before the label to make the action clearer, or after it to show forward movement. Icon-only buttons still need a label for screen readers.

examples.title: Toggle
examples.usage: A toggle that stays on, like Filters while the filter bar is open.
